interest: This file offers historians an illuminating look at the financial and structural reforms undertaken during the Allied Occupation of Japan, specifically the efforts to revive organized capital markets under American-style securities regulation. Despatches No. 324 and 325 capture the collision between SCAP's ambition to establish transparent, investor-oriented exchanges modeled on the U.S. SEC and the entrenched practices of Japanese brokers accustomed to wartime over-the-counter curb trading. A particularly compelling episode is the confidential investigation into market manipulation involving Norman Soong's Chinese Central News Agency, which circulated rumors that the State Department intended to purchase the Mitsui Main Building in order to depress Mitsui Real Estate stock. Furthermore, the file reveals the hand of prominent literary scholar Edward G. Seidensticker, Jr., who drafted both despatches during his early diplomatic career, while the inclusion of Robert A. Fearey's note on the 1946 land reform legislation illustrates the archival juxtapositions of occupation policy records.
keywords: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.5171) documents the resumption of securities exchange operations in Japan in May 1949 under the Allied Occupation, alongside an attached internal note on 1946 agricultural land reform legislation. The primary records consist of Tokyo Despatch No. 324 and confidential Despatch No. 325 from the Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, accompanied by SCAPIN 2004 from General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers. Together, they detail the reopening of stock exchanges in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya, the implementation of the new Securities and Exchanges Law (Law No. 25 of 1948), reaction across major Japanese newspapers, and internal SCAP concerns regarding market manipulation, speculative rumors concerning the Mitsui Main Building, and the disposition of Zaibatsu-held securities by the Holding Companies Liquidation Commission. A stray 1946 summary note by Robert A. Fearey regarding the Diet's passage of land reform laws is also included in the file bundle.

subfiles.about: Reports confidential comments by SCAP Economic and Scientific Section officials on the opening of Japanese stock exchanges and speculative rumors concerning the Mitsui Main Building.
subfiles.summary: This confidential despatch transmits observations from officials within SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section (ESS) regarding the reopening of stock exchanges in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya. Officials express doubt regarding the willingness and capability of Japanese securities dealers to comply with the newly instituted Securities and Exchanges Law. In particular, Securities Branch Chief L. A. Randall voices concern over false rumors circulated by Norman Soong's Chinese Central News Agency alleging that the U.S. State Department intended to purchase the Mitsui Main Building, likely designed to manipulate Mitsui Real Estate stock prices. ESS officials also assess that exchange trading will improve oversight and transaction reporting, though it is unlikely to accelerate the disposal of Zaibatsu-held securities by the Holding Companies Liquidation Commission.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 325: Comments Regarding Opening of Stock Exchanges

subfiles.about: Reports on the reopening of stock exchanges in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya, summarizes the provisions of the Securities and Exchanges Law, and reviews Japanese press commentary.
subfiles.summary: This unclassified despatch reports on the formal opening on May 14 and the start of trading on May 16, 1949, of securities exchanges in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya under SCAPIN 2004, noting upcoming applications for exchanges in Kobe, Kyoto, Hiroshima, Fukuoka, and Niigata. Initial trading saw modest volume but a sharp rise in heavy industrial shares like Japan Steel Manufacturing and Mitsubishi Heavy Industry following the U.S. announcement halting reparations removals. The despatch outlines the primary provisions of the Securities and Exchanges Law (Law No. 25 of 1948), including securities registration, dealer regulations, margin restrictions, and enforcement through a three-man Securities and Exchanges Commission. It also provides a detailed survey of Japanese press reactions from the Mainichi Shimbun, Tokyo Shimbun, Nihon Keizai Shimbun, and Asahi Shimbun discussing the transition away from curb operations and the challenges of curbing speculative activity.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 324: Opening of Stock Exchanges in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya

subfiles.about: Authorizes the Japanese Government to open securities exchanges in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya effective May 14, 1949, under SCAP controls.
subfiles.summary: This directive from General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers rescinds the earlier directive SCAPIN 59 of September 25, 1945. Acting upon a request from the Japanese Government's Central Liaison and Coordinating Office, it approves the opening of securities exchanges in Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya on May 14, 1949. All trading operations are subjected to SCAP controls, and the Japanese Government is instructed to submit separate requests for the future establishment or reopening of other securities and commodity exchanges.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2004: Memorandum on Securities Exchanges

subfiles.about: Summarizes the Revised Agricultural Land Adjustment Law and the Owner-Farmer Establishment Special Measure Law passed by the 90th Diet.
keywords: Special Measure for the Establishment of Owner-Farmer
subfiles.summary: This internal State Department memorandum by Robert A. Fearey notes the transmission of Despatch 909 enclosing copies of the Revised Agricultural Land Adjustment Law and the Bill for the Special Measure for the Establishment of Owner-Farmer. These companion statutes, passed by the 90th Diet in October 1946, form the cornerstone of Japan's postwar agricultural land reform program. The memorandum notes that an attached SCAP press release accurately outlines the core provisions of the land reform program as approved by the Cabinet and enacted by the Diet.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Agricultural Land Reform Laws (Despatch 909)
